subject: non-paired comparison with a reference file.

messages.author: e0f360daf21d20c0
messages.subject: non-paired comparison with a reference file.
parts:
Hello,

I would like to do a Copy-number-variation analysis between tumoral
SNP chips and a common reference file. This refecence file has been
created with the apt-copynumber-workflow program from 90 hapmap chips
(Affymetrix)
and is in HDF5 format.

I am looking for a way to process this setup with the aroma library,
but I did not find any existing function name. Does it exist?

thanks in advance for your help.

Rene Paradis

messages.author: 185f4d4fdb048fb8
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] non-paired comparison with a reference file.
parts:
On Thu, Dec 4, 2008 at 11:47 AM, ronmaster <rene.p...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Hello,
>
> I would like to do a Copy-number-variation analysis between tumoral
> SNP chips and a common reference file. This refecence file has been
> created with the apt-copynumber-workflow program from 90 hapmap chips
> (Affymetrix)
> and is in HDF5 format.
>
> I am looking for a way to process this setup with the aroma library,
> but I did not find any existing function name. Does it exist?

There is no such function in aroma.affymetrix. You'll have to find an
function/package in R that can read HDF5 files, figure out the file
format of that file, the understand the file format of
aroma.affymetrix chip effect CEL file, and the import from one to the
other.

A much easier way is to download the HapMap samples and process it in
aroma.affymetrix. You'll end up with a normalized chip effect set,
say 'cesN' and then you take the robust average of those by

ceR <- getAverage(cesN)

which I guess will correspond to that pre-generated reference of APT.

Also, this is approach is probably better because this pooled
reference is generated using the same preprocessing method that you
later will use for your own samples.

Finally, unless you have less than 15-20 samples, I do not recommend
using an external data set as a reference. The across lab effect will
probably add more noise than what you will gain. I've mentioned this,
and others reported the same, in earlier threads on aroma.affymetrix
mailing list (search archive online).

Cheers

Henrik
